newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast prods flat to lower, buyers vanish.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast prods flat to lower, buyers vanish.

text.p: Prices for U.S. West Coast refined products stayed flat to lower Tuesday, as buyers stopped trading to see how low energy futures would drop in New York, market players said.
At 1123 PDT (1923 GMT), May crude oil on New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) eased 48 cents a barrel to $19.90 as traders sold their contracts before they expire today.
May gasoline, which expires April 30, fell 0.85 cents a gallon to 61.95 cents a gallon.
"All the buyers are running away with the Merc (New York Mercantile Exchange) doing what it's doing," a trader said.
April/May prices for CARB (California Air Resources Board) unleaded gasoline in Los Angeles were talked one cent lower than Monday at 71 to 72 cents.
Two cargoes of CARB were slated to arrive this week, but traders did not immediately know when they would come.
L.A. low sulphur diesel offers dropped 1.50 cents a gallon to 59.50 cents, amid rumors of an incoming cargo.
